## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gahapatijātaka* (Ja 199), titled *The Householder* in English, is a narrative discourse in the Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to the traditional framing narrative, the Buddha recounted the story during his stay at Jetavana concerning a backsliding monk (*ukkaṇṭhita bhikkhu*) [Fausböll 1879]. Observing that womankind cannot easily be kept upright and will invariably err and deceive their husbands (*mātugāmo nāma arakkhiyo, pāpaṁ katvā yena ten' upāyena sāmikaṁ vañceti yevā*), the Buddha introduced the tale of the past (*atītaṁ āhari*), which opens with the verse phrase *Ubhayam me na khamati* ("I like not this") [Fausböll 1879].
